title: Foundations: Gospel Bluegrass - The Complete Guide
summary: What Gospel Bluegrass is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Gospel Bluegrass songs: Bluegrass is acoustic music at full sprint: banjo, mandolin, fiddle, guitar, and bass playing breakneck tempos with stacked harmonies. Bill Monroe invented it in the 1940s; nobody has slowed it down since.

History: Bill Monroe and the Blue Grass Boys (named for Kentucky) created the form; Flatt & Scruggs (Earl Scruggs's three-finger banjo) popularized it. The 1960s folk revival and O Brother made it mainstream again.

How the songs work: Gospel Bluegrass favors the keys of G, C, D, A, Bb. Common forms include Verse-chorus with instrumental breaks between every verse; High lonesome stacked harmonies. Players should master scruggs-style three-finger banjo rolls first, then the g-run: banjo lick ending every break. Banjo capo and spikes for key changes.

title: In the Pines (Where Did You Sleep Last Night) - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for In the Pines (Where Did You Sleep Last Night), a public-domain Gospel Bluegrass standard.
body:
In the Pines (Where Did You Sleep Last Night) (Traditional American, 19th century. Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
My girl, my girl, don't lie to me,
Tell me where did you sleep last night?
In the pines, in the pines,
Where the sun don't ever shine,
I would shiver the whole night through.

Her husband was a hard-working man,
Just about a mile from here,
His head was found in a driving wheel,
But his body never was found.

My girl, my girl, don't lie to me,
Tell me where did you sleep last night?
In the pines, in the pines,
Where the sun don't ever shine,
I would shiver the whole night through.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Gospel Bluegrass accompaniment in G using the 'Bluegrass I–IV–V' pattern:
G | C | D | G

Technique: scruggs-style three-finger banjo rolls. Banjo capo and spikes for key changes.

title: Blue Moon of Kentucky - Gospel Bluegrass Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Blue Moon of Kentucky by Bill Monroe (1946).
body:
Blue Moon of Kentucky — Bill Monroe, 1946. The bluegrass national anthem; Elvis covered it.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of D):
Dm | C | Dm | C

This study chart uses the 'Minor modal i–VII' progression, the Gospel Bluegrass workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: verse-chorus with instrumental breaks between every verse. Listen for mandolin chop on the backbeat — it is the fingerprint of the style.
